title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #14

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In a singing game, who gives the instructions? (1 mark)
   A. The audience only
   B. The soloist
   C. Nobody
   D. The oldest pupil always

2. Which of these words is a noun? (1 mark)
   A. boil
   B. slowly
   C. tasty
   D. millet

3. Why do we keep a class portfolio of songs? (1 mark)
   A. To hide them
   B. So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   C. To sell them
   D. To throw them away

4. Which is a clue that a noun is plural? (1 mark)
   A. The word the
   B. A full stop
   C. A capital letter
   D. A number word such as three before it

5. What is a good first step when reading for information? (1 mark)
   A. Close the book
   B. Guess the ending
   C. Copy the title
   D. Ask what you want to find out

6. A sentence should begin with (1 mark)
   A. a small drawing
   B. a comma
   C. a capital letter
   D. a number

7. What is a gallery walk in handwriting practice? (1 mark)
   A. A test of running
   B. A race in the field
   C. A song
   D. Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display

8. Which of these is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. The door was open.
   B. A door has a handle.
   C. The door is red.
   D. Close the door.

9. Which game teaches that messages can change when passed on? (1 mark)
   A. Chinese whisper
   B. Football
   C. Skipping
   D. Hide and seek only

10. A newsreader on the radio should speak (1 mark)
   A. in a whisper
   B. very fast
   C. with no pauses
   D. clearly and at a steady pace

11. How can recording your reading help you? (1 mark)
   A. It makes you forget
   B. It ends practice
   C. You can listen back and see how to improve
   D. It deletes the story

12. Which of these must always begin with a capital letter in English? (1 mark)
   A. The names of foods
   B. The names of people
   C. The names of weather
   D. The names of colours

13. The word I is always written (1 mark)
   A. as a small letter
   B. with a comma
   C. as a capital letter
   D. in brackets

14. What is the guessing language game with verbs? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   B. Pupils read a book
   C. Pupils write verbs on the board silently
   D. Pupils sing nouns

15. Why should you look back at the dialogue when answering questions? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the page
   B. To find accurate answers
   C. To copy a friend
   D. To waste time

16. What should you do when a stranger offers you a lift? (1 mark)
   A. Say no politely and tell a trusted adult
   B. Go with them
   C. Accept sweets
   D. Give your name

17. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a picture
   B. a song
   C. a conversation between two or more people
   D. a long poem

18. What should you put after a starting word such as First? (1 mark)
   A. A comma
   B. A colon
   C. Nothing
   D. A question mark

19. A good storyteller (1 mark)
   A. forgets the ending
   B. reads without looking
   C. practises and speaks clearly
   D. whispers all the time

20. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A type of number
   B. A very long story
   C. A page of a book
   D. A short wise saying that gives advice

21. What does A stitch in time saves nine mean? (1 mark)
   A. Fix small problems early
   B. Stitches are costly
   C. Sewing is easy
   D. Nine is a lucky number

22. Why might a class record narrations on a device? (1 mark)
   A. To listen back and improve
   B. To waste time
   C. To sell them
   D. To erase them

23. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of shop
   B. Money spent
   C. A bill
   D. Money left after paying the cost

24. What is a vocabulary bank? (1 mark)
   A. A place for money
   B. A book cover
   C. A kind of poem
   D. A list of useful words on a theme

25. Which group of words is a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Fifty shillings
   B. The customer in the market
   C. Pays fifty
   D. The customer pays fifty shillings.

26. What is a bargain? (1 mark)
   A. To discuss the price
   B. To steal
   C. To run
   D. To sleep

27. The goat is inside the shed. Which preposition shows this? (1 mark)
   A. between
   B. in
   C. behind
   D. outside

28. What is animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. Selling animals only
   B. Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   C. Ignoring animals
   D. Hunting animals

29. Which is an example of caring for an animal? (1 mark)
   A. Beating it
   B. Throwing stones at it
   C. Giving clean water every day
   D. Leaving it without shelter

30. How should you read a sad poem? (1 mark)
   A. Without a pause
   B. Slowly and softly
   C. Fast and loudly
   D. Laughing

31. In choral recitation, the group (1 mark)
   A. reads silently
   B. sings only
   C. writes the poem
   D. says the poem together at the same pace

32. What is the problem in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The ending word
   C. The page
   D. The trouble or challenge the characters face

33. What is a motion in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. The statement the teams discuss
   B. A dance
   C. A song
   D. A gift

34. Which of these is an adjective in Fresh sweet oranges? (1 mark)
   A. sale
   B. oranges
   C. sweet
   D. for

35. Which describes an object by size and colour? (1 mark)
   A. Bagging
   B. A big red bag
   C. To bag
   D. A bag

36. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. The last word
   B. A picture
   C. A short eye-catching title
   D. A price

37. Which field asks how old you are? (1 mark)
   A. Signature
   B. Age
   C. Class
   D. School

38. Which pair of verbs shows an action? (1 mark)
   A. vote, count
   B. is, are
   C. table, chair
   D. red, blue

39. What is a poem's title? (1 mark)
   A. Its page
   B. Its last line
   C. Its rhyme
   D. Its name

40. What does a red eight-sided road sign tell drivers? (1 mark)
   A. Go faster
   B. Stop
   C. Park
   D. Turn left

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. What is a verb? Give two examples. (2 marks)

42. Explain the difference between a simile and a metaphor and give an example of each. (4 marks)

43. Write a five-sentence oral paragraph about a free day. Include three interjections that show different feelings. (5 marks)

44. Write three sentences describing where things are in your classroom. Use a different preposition in each. (3 marks)

45. Give three parts of a news item. (3 marks)

46. State three steps for writing a dialogue. (3 marks)

47. Write a five-line role play dialogue on personal safety between a child and a stranger. Show the speaker names and use question marks correctly. (5 marks)

48. Write an advert of four sentences for hand-made baskets. Include a headline, two adjectives, a price and where to buy. (5 marks)

49. Explain what turn taking means. (2 marks)

50. Compose a four-line poem about a good leader. Make lines two and four rhyme. (4 marks)

51. Read: Fire can be dangerous. Never play with matches. Ask an adult to light the stove. If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. State the main idea and list three details. (5 marks)

52. Explain what a dialogue is. (2 marks)

53. Name two parts of an advert. (2 marks)

54. Give two rules for filling in a form correctly. (2 marks)

55. Write two sentences using the interjections Hurray and Ouch. (2 marks)

56. Explain what a stanza is. (2 marks)

57. Describe how you would scan a passage to find how much a box of mangoes costs. (4 marks)

58. Name two components of a poem. (2 marks)

59. State three steps for reading your part in a dialogue. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The soloist
   The soloist leads by singing the instructions and the group responds.

2. D — millet
   Millet is a grain, so it names a thing. The others are an action, a describing word and an adverb.

3. B — So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   A portfolio preserves the songs collected from the community.

4. D — A number word such as three before it
   Number words show how many there are.

5. D — Ask what you want to find out
   A question in mind helps you look for the right facts.

6. C — a capital letter
   Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

7. D — Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
   Pupils view and comment on displayed work.

8. D — Close the door.
   Close the door tells you what to do.

9. A — Chinese whisper
   In Chinese whisper the message changes as it passes.

10. D — clearly and at a steady pace
   News should be clear and easy to follow.

11. C — You can listen back and see how to improve
   Playing back shows where to improve.

12. B — The names of people
   Names of people and places begin with capital letters.

13. C — as a capital letter
   In English the word I is always a capital.

14. A — Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   Acting helps everyone connect verbs with actions.

15. B — To find accurate answers
   Answers should come from the text.

16. A — Say no politely and tell a trusted adult
   Personal safety means not going with strangers.

17. C — a conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue records people speaking to each other.

18. A — A comma
   We usually put a comma after First at the start of a sentence.

19. C — practises and speaks clearly
   Practice and clarity make a good teller.

20. D — A short wise saying that gives advice
   Proverbs teach lessons in a few words.

21. A — Fix small problems early
   Early action prevents bigger trouble.

22. A — To listen back and improve
   Recordings show what to improve.

23. D — Money left after paying the cost
   Profit is gain after costs.

24. D — A list of useful words on a theme
   A word bank stores words to learn.

25. D — The customer pays fifty shillings.
   It has a subject and a predicate.

26. A — To discuss the price
   Bargaining is agreeing on price.

27. B — in
   In shows something is inside.

28. B — Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   Welfare means care for animals' well-being.

29. C — Giving clean water every day
   Water and shelter meet its needs.

30. B — Slowly and softly
   Slow and soft matches sadness.

31. D — says the poem together at the same pace
   Choral means together.

32. D — The trouble or challenge the characters face
   The problem drives the events.

33. A — The statement the teams discuss
   The motion is the topic.

34. C — sweet
   Sweet describes the oranges.

35. B — A big red bag
   Big and red are adjectives.

36. C — A short eye-catching title
   A headline is the title of an advert or news item.

37. B — Age
   Age records how old you are.

38. A — vote, count
   Vote and count are actions.

39. D — Its name
   The title names the poem.

40. B — Stop
   That shape is the stop sign.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: A verb is an action word. Examples: run, close, bring, put.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for two correct examples.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A simile compares using like or as, for example as quick as lightning. A metaphor says one thing is another, for example Time is money.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition and one for each example.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five sentences with three suitable interjections such as Hurray, Wow and Oops used to show joy, surprise and a mistake.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for three suitable interjections shown correctly.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example The board is in front of the class. My bag is under my desk. The teacher stands beside the door.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Headline, lead, details, quote (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Choose theme, choose characters, decide setting, write each speaker on a new line, use interjections, read aloud.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five correct lines, for example Child: Good afternoon. Stranger: Do you want a ride? Child: No, thank you. I will wait for my mother. Stranger: Are you sure? Child: Yes, I am telling my teacher.
   Working / marking points: One mark for speaker names, one for a safe message, one for correct questions and two for five clear lines.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any advert with a headline, two adjectives, a price and a place, for example: Strong Baskets for Sale. Our baskets are big and colourful. Only 300 shillings each. Buy at the market gate.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the four required features and one mark for clear sentences.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means speaking one person at a time and waiting for others to finish before speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for one at a time and one for waiting.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on leadership with two rhyming lines, for example A good leader listens, Speaks the truth each day, Helps the weak and lonely, And shows the proper way.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme and four lines, two marks for rhyme.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Main idea: Fire is dangerous and needs care. Details: never play with matches, ask an adult to light the stove, stop drop and roll.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the main idea and one mark for each of three details.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people, shown with each speaker's name and words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for speakers.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Headline, picture, description, price, contact details (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Read instructions first, write neatly inside the spaces, give true information, sign and date it (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hurray! We won the match. Ouch! I hurt my foot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, separated from the next group by a space.
   Working / marking points: One mark for group of lines and one for separation.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Know that you are looking for the price, run your eyes over the text looking for numbers, stop at the number, read the sentence around it and check that it answers the question.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, message (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, underline your lines, practise them, watch the punctuation, wait for your cue.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.
